result_text:
I added `DataStore.findOverduePurchaseOrdersOfSupplier(long supplierId, LocalDate date)` in `src/main/java/com/acme/backoffice/DataStore.java`, next to the other overdue finders. `OpenPurchaseOrdersTest` passes with the new test.

It returns the supplier's sent purchase orders whose expected date is before the given date. They come back earliest expected date first, then by id, each with its order lines. It reuses the existing `overdueOn(date)` query filtered by supplier, so draft, received and cancelled orders are excluded and an order expected on the date itself is not overdue.

The new test is `overdueOrdersOfOneSupplierAreBeforeTheGivenDate` in `src/test/java/com/acme/backoffice/OpenPurchaseOrdersTest.java`. It covers your 13 July example: orders expected 8 July (two) and 12 July are listed in that order, and one expected 20 July is not. It also covers the boundary date, another supplier's orders, and an unknown supplier.

I only ran that one test class, not the full suite. I didn't add a service method, because the existing purchase-order finders aren't exposed through one.
